key_insight: Transient absorption in CH3NH3PbBr3 is governed by electronic effects at femtosecond timescales and by thermal lattice effects at picosecond timescales, which can be disentangled with first-principles modeling.
engineering_relevance: The result clarifies how pump-probe signatures should be interpreted in perovskite devices, improving diagnostics of carrier dynamics and lattice heating in solar-cell materials.
method: Nonequilibrium Bethe-Salpeter equation for excited-state spectra
Ab initio molecular dynamics for finite-temperature lattice motion
Combined analysis of X-ray and optical transient absorption
evidence_signal: The abstract reports quantitative agreement across femtosecond-to-picosecond timescales, showing electronic dominance early and distinct lattice-driven spectral changes later.
watch_item: The conclusions are material- and timescale-specific, so applying them to other perovskites or experimental conditions may require recalibration of the excited-state and temperature-dependent model.
paper_title: Disentangling Electronic and Lattice Contributions to Transient Absorption in Metal Halide Perovskites: A First-Principles Study of CH3NH3PbBr3
